messages.subject: Proposal: a free tier as a growth lever
messages.body:
Hi all!

Quick idea while the launch is top of mind: a free tier. Tiny plan - 1 vehicle, 2 drivers, basic tracking only - permanently free, no card required. The playbook is well proven in our category: free tier feeds the top of the funnel, product-led growth, self-serve upgrade path when small couriers hit the limits. Right now if you're a two-van operation you look at our pricing page and bounce!

I've sketched a funnel model (attached: 'Free tier funnel model v1') - conservatively it could add 80-120 signups/month, and even a 3% conversion is meaningful ARR at our price points.

Would love to get this into the Q3 planning conversation!

Chloe 🚀

messages.subject: RE: Proposal: a free tier as a growth lever
messages.body:
Dear Chloe,

Thank you for the model - I have read it with interest, though I must be honest and say I remain sceptical. A few observations:

1. Free accounts are not free to serve. Even one vehicle and two drivers means infra, support tickets, and a billing record that never bills. At your 80-120 signups per month, that is a permanently growing cost base, most of which I would expect never to convert.
2. Your 3% conversion assumption appears to be based on general industry benchmarks rather than anything specific to courier operators, who I would gently suggest are more cost-conscious and stickier than the average SaaS SMB.
3. We have 310 paying accounts. A free tier could also cannibalise the Starter plan, which we only just repositioned in February; if 10 prospective Starter customers a month take the free tier instead, the maths changes considerably.
4. Free riders may also attract abuse - duplicate accounts to stay within limits - which is another support and billing burden.

I am not saying no, but I would want a much firmer conversion estimate and a support-cost model before this went anywhere near a plan.

Kind regards,
Helen Oyelaran
Chief Financial Officer, Parcelwise B.V.

messages.subject: RE: Proposal: a free tier as a growth lever
messages.body:
Quick recap of where I sit:

1. Neutral. I can see both sides - Helen's cost point is real, and so is Chloe's top-of-funnel point
2. My instinct is that anything new goes after the rollout is done and we see what v3 does to conversions organically
3. If it is ever seriously considered, I would want it scoped by product first (what exactly is metered, abuse limits, upgrade triggers) rather than agreed as a marketing concept

No strong opinion either way at this stage.

Thanks!
Priya

messages.subject: RE: Proposal: a free tier as a growth lever
messages.body:
All fair points! I'll sharpen the model - I'll try to get real conversion data from a couple of comparable companies in our network and a rough support-ticket-per-free-account estimate, and come back with a version that answers Helen's maths. Priya, once the launch settles I'll bring you the scoping questions so product and marketing are on the same page!

Chloe

messages.subject: RE: Proposal: a free tier as a growth lever
messages.body:
Gentle nudge - I never found great comparable conversion data (nobody wants to share their numbers, shocking!), so I've parked the model for now. Picking it up again after the rollout review, unless anyone feels differently!

Chloe
